truthBoundary: Real measurements taken for teaching (plan §1 item 9). Not a validated entropy source, not an ESV submission, and no min-entropy claim about these devices beyond what the estimator output shows for each dataset under its recorded conditions.

sampleFormat.gcdReduction: none: the recorder does not call jent_entropy_init(), so jent_gcd_get() reports no GCD and jent_entropy_collector_alloc_internal() sets jent_common_timer_gcd = 1 (src/jitterentropy-base.c:652-658); values are undivided timer deltas
sampleFormat.restartSemantics: jitterentropy-hashtime <1000> <1000> loops 1000 times in ONE process, each time calling jent_one_test(), which allocates a new entropy collector, primes it with one jent_measure_jitter() call, records 1000 deltas and frees it. It is upstream's restart procedure (invoke_testing_helper.sh raw_entropy_restart), not a power cycle or process restart.
sampleFormat.restartMatrixLayout: row-major 1000 × 1000: byte (r-1)*1000 + (c-1) = restart r, sample c (0-based offset)

notCollected.why: No reachable interface on any of the three devices (i.MX 95 ELE TRNG: /dev/hwrng output only; KV260: none; Mac: none). Per the user decision, no new noise source was built.
/dev/hwrng is not present inside the docker container; not pursued (it would be host-supplied output anyway).
Needs root (powermetrics); sudo not available to the collector. pmset thermal-warning state recorded instead.
The Mac was running other sessions' workloads throughout (load average 33-60 before the run). The 'idle' Mac and OrbStack datasets are a shared-host baseline and are labelled as such.

Failed because BusyBox 'head' has no -c option (0-byte file). Retried at 03:13:03Z with dd; the failed files are not shipped. The retry ran about 40 s after the loaded run ended (a55-thermal 62.5 C), not under a defined idle/loaded condition.

nativeReference.platform: native-arm64-strict: linux/arm64, Debian trixie, g++ 14.2, upstream flags + -ffp-contract=off (the W1 parity reference)
notes: non-IID values: every estimator field of the tool JSON; native-arm64-strict produced identical JSON and stdout to the WASM build.
IID values: only the deterministic fields. The permutation test is seeded by the tool from /dev/urandom, so its counters vary run to run; verdicts are those seen over the unseeded parity runs.
restart values: runs with a pinned /dev/urandom. The sanity-check cutoff X_cutoff is a Monte-Carlo quantile, so a learner run may print a different X_cutoff.
